why: Many-to-one is the same FK pattern viewed from the child — reinforcing that cardinality is about perspective, not a different physical mechanism.
pitfalls: Thinking N:1 needs a different FK placement than 1:N — it does not.
teachAlong: Cause: many children point at one parent.
Effect: same FK pattern; wording is from the child view.
mappingNotes: Compare your ORM/schema code with the Equivalent SQL panel. The task gate introspects Postgres — only real tables/FKs count.
solution:
from sqlalchemy import String, Integer, Numeric, Boolean, ForeignKey, UniqueConstraint, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

from decimal import Decimal


class LabCustomer(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_customers"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200), unique=True)


class LabOrder(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_orders"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    total: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(Numeric(10, 2))
    customer_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("lab_customers.id"))
    customer: Mapped["LabCustomer"] = relationship()

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
